title: What our methods can and cannot do: the abstract rounds
made_with: AI agents (Claude) directed by the author

findings.statement: The algebra of combining units (side by side, and nesting a block-k unit inside a block-m unit) has one dimension: every monotone homomorphism is n -> n^theta for a single theta, or degenerate. So the best saving s* is one number whatever block sizes are used (Theorem C).
findings.status_detail: an independent AI skeptic re-derived it and found no error; no person and no proof checker has checked it (one skeptic)

findings.statement: Every certificate meets the saving through one growth exponent per block, theta(psi) = min_j ln(psi_m/psi_j)/ln(m/j); a certificate with growth exponent theta rules out savings above 1 - theta and no more (Lemma D); mixing certificates never beats the best single one (Lemma E). To rule out a saving of 0.1 a family needs growth exponent >= 0.9 at arbitrarily large blocks; a family never proving more than 4 moves per array cannot rule out 0.1 at any block >= 5.
findings.status_detail: an independent AI skeptic re-derived it and found no error; no person and no proof checker has checked it (one skeptic); the skeptic corrected 'at every block' to 'at arbitrarily large blocks'

findings.statement: One direction costs at most two calls of the whole block transform: dir_e1 = S1 K S1 K^-1 S1^3 exactly, K^-1 = K X_all.
findings.status_detail: exact computation in Q(i) at blocks 1 to 3, one program, not repeated by anyone; argued by hand for every block

findings.statement: Units whose mixing coefficients never divide by 2 never save, at any block, in any composition (Proposition G: the mod-2 frame distance is a perfect certificate).
findings.status_detail: assembles two results of the earlier revisions; no skeptic read the assembly

findings.statement: Growth exponents of the start lifts are 0.85, 0.71, 0.57 and 0.44 at blocks 3 to 6; at engine prices for grouped blocks lifts cap the saving near 0.43 at block 5 (hooks: 0.83) and near 0.56 at block 6.
findings.status_detail: exact at blocks 3 and 4, exact edges plus sampled pairs at block 5, sampled at block 6; one AI skeptic recomputed the block-4 pair sums exactly over 2,632,365 pairs and enlarged the block-6 sample (growth exponent about 0.437)
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: identical at blocks 3 and 4 (apart from the input path); blocks 5 and 6 not re-run

findings.statement: Ceilings flow up the ladder of games: a certificate for a game with more free steps is a certificate, with the same numbers, for every game below it, so a ceiling computed in the engine game holds in every game above it.
findings.status_detail: two independent AI skeptics re-derived it and found no error; no person and no proof checker has checked it

findings.statement: In the engine game a certificate loses nothing by ignoring Pauli flips (Theorem 1), so every engine certificate is a pattern of subspaces on the frames; the hook's frame pattern alone gives 14/5 at block 3 (on all 18,090 ordered frame pairs it takes one value per distance: 80, 144, 224 at distances 1, 2, 3; 224/80 = 14/5).
findings.status_detail: an independent AI skeptic re-derived it and found no error; no person and no proof checker has checked it (one skeptic); the frame-pair values are checked by computer

findings.statement: In the everything-free game every certificate of the usual product form must ignore everything, so it proves nothing (Theorem 2; rests on Tof X0 Tof^-1 = X0 CNOT(1->2) and CS X0 CS^-1 = X0 S1 CZ).
findings.status_detail: an independent AI skeptic re-derived it and found no error; no person and no proof checker has checked it (one skeptic)

findings.statement: Colourings and coordinate frame families have ceilings 1.75 (block 3), 1.875 (block 4), below 2 at every block in the engine game, and 21/16 at block 3 and below 4/3 in the chi game (Proposition 3).
findings.status_detail: an independent AI skeptic re-derived it and found no error; no person and no proof checker has checked it (one skeptic)

findings.statement: Theorem S': every cut (certificate built from non-repeated irreducible pieces) at block m proves fewer than 4(2^m - 1)/(2^m + 1) moves per array: 12/5, 28/9, 60/17, 124/33, 252/65 at blocks 2 to 6, below 4 always. So no certificate without repeated pieces can settle the bar at any block from 5 on.
findings.status_detail: two independent AI skeptics re-derived it and found no error; no person and no proof checker has checked it

findings.statement: All 24,609 cuts of the 30 irreducibles of Sp(6,2) were computed; none beats the hook's 14/5, which is a cut in the 56-dimensional irreducible; the eigenvalue ratio 5/14 appears in 29 of the 30.
findings.status_detail: one program, not repeated by anyone
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: not re-run (needs the 228 MB cache of irreducibles)

findings.statement: Theorem M: in the 105-dimensional irreducible 105a of Sp(6,2) (value -35 on transvections), the sum of the weight spaces of one 28-element orbit (dimension 56) has profile (20, 38, 49) against the hook's (10, 18, 28); with Theorem R it excludes the block-3 mixed units 1+4 in 10, 2+8 in 20, 4+21 in 49 and 7+38 in 88 in the engine game; the engine room for mixed units falls from 0.1255 to 0.1160.
findings.status_detail: exact computation; two independent AI skeptics repeated it with their own code; the two skeptics each rebuilt the certificate in a different model (through W(E7)); it does not apply in the widened game

findings.statement: Mixed units have more room than pure ones at block 3 (Schoenhage's tau-theorem transplanted): room 0.1255 against 0.0628 for a pure kernel and 0.079 for pure rank-2 targets, from a sweep of 180 certificates.
findings.status_detail: exact computation; an independent AI skeptic repeated it with its own code (one skeptic)

findings.statement: A Venn certificate in Lambda^3 V (x) Lambda^4 V with intersection pattern {0,2} has cap 752 (exact) and rank-2 demand 1424: rank-2 targets with one spare row need at least 89/47 = 1.8936 moves each, which excludes 7 in 13, 8 in 15 and 9 in 17 at block 3 in the widened game (hence the engine game); 10 in 19 (0.074) is the smallest open case.
findings.status_detail: exact computation; an independent AI skeptic repeated it with its own code (one skeptic); the cap is exact over Q, the demands are ranks modulo two primes (lower bounds)

findings.statement: Every whole-graph block-3 lift has excess at least 68 on its 945 edges (Lemma E3: an interval lift with a bad end edge costs at least 3, attained by an exact lift; 64 end and 96 middle incidences per edge), so every block-3 lift proves at most 2835/1013 = 2.7986 moves per array, below the hook; no lift can exclude 5 in 14 or 6 in 17.
findings.status_detail: two independent AI skeptics re-derived it and found no error; no person and no proof checker has checked it; the counts are checked by computer

findings.statement: Every block-4 interval lift has excess at least 18 (exact LP dual 120/7; ILP optimum 18), so 18 <= b_4 <= 36; block 5 has at least 141 (dual 5611/40); excess per edge is at least 0.072 from block 3 and 0.075 from block 4.
findings.status_detail: exact computation; two independent AI skeptics repeated it with their own code (exact LP dual certificates)
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: block 4 identical apart from the last digits of the float LP value; block 5 not re-run

findings.statement: Decomposed block-4 lifts need exactly 36 on an interval, so they prove at most 80/23 = 3.478 moves per array at block 4, just under 4^0.9 = 3.482.
findings.status_detail: exhaustive search over 32 million sets of lines by the first-cycle lifts track; used and not refuted by the second wave's two skeptics, but not re-derived

findings.statement: Theorem SG: through the Dvir-Saraf-Wigderson rank bound, decomposed lifts pay at least (2/3)kappa_m per edge, tending to about 1/3 at large even blocks and 0.314 at large odd ones, effective only from about block 110.
findings.status_detail: two independent AI skeptics re-derived it and found no error; no person and no proof checker has checked it

findings.statement: Every Sylvester-Gallai-type counting argument is capped at exactly 1/3 per edge, so the bar's threshold overtakes it from block 18 (Proposition C).
findings.status_detail: both skeptics of the lifts track; what survives: the cap is some constant ((2/3)kappa_m = 0.400, 0.583, 0.299, 0.387 at blocks 3-6 for the linear version; at least 0.38 for a sharper version; about 1 for the whole class), so such counting can never show that lifts fail at all large blocks
findings.refuted_by: skeptics' recomputation of the LP and counterexample phi = 1/6 to the forced end rows

findings.statement: Theorem F and the angle law: for any frame-family certificate at blocks up to 40 the spectral factor from edges to depth j is at most 2 - 2^(1-j), the exact maximum there; at larger blocks only a cap of 8/3 is shown, and the ratio at depth j is spectral factor times angle factor s_1/s_j. Theorem H: hooks use the full spectral factor at every depth, block and k, so their value is their angle factor, below 2; every hook has right-angle edges. Settling the bar at block m <= 40 needs angle factor >= m^0.9/2 (2.88 at block 7, 3.97 at block 10); every family computed stays below 2.
findings.status_detail: two independent AI skeptics re-derived it and found no error; no person and no proof checker has checked it; the skeptics added s_1 = 1 for every hook and the exact 68,320

findings.statement: The block-4 near miss (2 in 7, private-end branch) is one number: under the k = 8 hook a move is worth at most 27,456 and a depth-3 piece needs 68,320 (exact over Q), leaving 640 of 137,280; the hook has full spectral factor 7/4 and right-angle edges, and its depth-3 average sin^2 per angle is 48,048/68,320 = 0.7033; closing needs a certificate whose depth-3 average is below 0.7 times its edge average.
findings.status_detail: exact computation; two independent AI skeptics repeated it with their own code

findings.statement: A search of about 4,000 block-4 certificates (hook relatives; cuts of the Sp(8,2) irreducibles 85, 238, 510, 595; all 2,047 orbit cuts; overlap cuts) found none above the hook's 2135/858 = 2.488 at depth 3; the named irreducibles reach only 13/7, 9/4, 11/6, 7/3; the block-4 hook ties several pieces together; building from block 3 would need a block-3 certificate above 2.849.
findings.status_detail: one AI skeptic repeated the main result with its own code (hook numbers mod two primes, orbit cuts, overlap cuts by a different reduction) and computed the 22 missing orbit cuts (best 2.304); hook-relative runners-up 2.4868, 2.4858, 2.4855 not rechecked
findings.rerun_2026_10_19: proj_counts.py re-run; the searches not re-run

findings.statement: A certificate with the full spectral factor 7/4 and depth-3 average sin^2 below 0.7 closes the near-miss branch.
findings.status_detail: orbit cut 1434 has spectral factor 7/4 and s_3 = 0.699 but s_1 = 858/865 and misses (2.483); the correct test is s_3 < 0.7 s_1
findings.refuted_by: the cert-07 skeptic's orbit cut 1434 (and its mirror 854)

findings.statement: In the chi game at block 3 every certificate is capped at 169/57 = 2.965 moves per array; natively an exact 13-row certificate of rank inequalities (5 submodularity, 4 monotonicity, 3 Ingleton, 1 Dougherty-Freiling-Zeger) on the 44-frame interval over F_4 proves it, with one Fano gadget of weight 2/57; the 360 Fano planes buy nothing. The three open thresholds 8/3, 5/2, 7/3 lie inside the window (231/131, 169/57].
findings.status_detail: exact computation; two independent AI skeptics repeated it with their own code; both routes rest on an earlier reduction (all certificates to rank inequalities on one interval) that no skeptic has checked

findings.statement: Chi-game lifts survive locally by 0.006: the least excess of a 44-frame interval lift is between 9 (exact; 12 is a solver bound with Hirzebruch rows) and 18 (an exact lift whose 9 bad edges are the tangent flags of the Hermitian curve), so the local ceiling 147/55 = 2.6727 is above 8/3; every chi-game lift proves at most 147/52 = 2.827 (2.774 if the solver bound 12 holds); a whole-geometry lift excludes 3 in 8 only with excess at most 2,338 on 18,711 edges (best known 13,122).
findings.status_detail: exact computation; two independent AI skeptics repeated it with their own code

findings.statement: In the chi game no cut proves more than 28/11 = 2.545 (from the 891-frame graph's degree 42 and second eigenvalue 9), so no cut can exclude 3 in 8 there.
findings.status_detail: no skeptic has read it; the eigenvalue arithmetic is checked by computer

findings.statement: Theorem E+: the sign defect of the earlier transfer vanishes identically and the naive collapse of Clifford cellular automata is multiplicative, so every certificate kept by monomial Clifford tensor powers gives the same bounds (2W at block 2, 14W/5 at block 3, 41W/13 at block 4) in every game whose letters are locality-preserving Clifford maps with translation-invariant bulk (unimodular chain maps, CZ and i-phase couplings, cyclic rotations, boundary Cliffords) and whose free letters are monomial or boundary-local.
findings.status_detail: an independent AI skeptic re-derived it and found no error; no person and no proof checker has checked it (one skeptic); randomized exact checks on 1,440 automata and 720 pairs with a control that has power

findings.statement: Theorem X: a formally polynomial approximate unit (cancellations of negative eps-powers hold with the paid moves as unknown symbols) runs exactly at a cost factor O(log log N), so its saving is unchanged.
findings.status_detail: an independent AI skeptic re-derived it and found no error; no person and no proof checker has checked it (one skeptic)

findings.statement: Making a relation-using approximate unit exact costs at least a factor 2 per level, so such units are worthless at blocks 2 to 4.
findings.status_detail: the skeptic's toy counterexample needs 3 coefficient-level paid calls for M = 3, and 1 after pruning: the factor can be 1; the cost lies between the exact cost and (a+1)M

findings.statement: A family of approximate units gives a real unit only if its error is exactly zero in the limit (transfer criterion).
findings.status_detail: counterexample: scale by 1 + 1/k; exact units form a closed set, so every bounded family whose error tends to 0 has an exact limit; only families with unbounded numbers can fail

findings.statement: One array needs m paid moves in every game whose free steps do bounded work per output entry (chi and everything-free games included); without sums of arrays no circuit goes below m paid moves per array (ZX track, after the repair p f + 2mWL >= mWf for every f, so p >= mW).
findings.status_detail: upheld by AI skeptics in two rounds; the ZX version was refuted as first written (its premise that every free step permutes and rephases entries is false with Hadamards on end columns) and both ZX skeptics supplied the repair

findings.statement: PyZX 0.10.7's basic_optimization changes the linear map of circuits containing XPhase gates; minimal failing input CNOT(2,1), CNOT(1,2), XPhase(1, phase 1/2) on 3 qubits.
findings.status_detail: exact computation; an independent AI skeptic repeated it with its own code (one skeptic)

findings.statement: GCT: the best closed (GCT-type) obstruction proves exactly the border complexity and is capped by the same barrier as rank methods; an obstruction seeing only some irreducibles is capped by a computable relaxed game; irreducibles couple only through shared P_0-types.
findings.status_detail: no skeptic has read it

findings.statement: At block 3, inside the hook's 56-dimensional irreducible, an exact 5 in 14 and an exact mixed 1+4 in 10 exist in the relaxed game (residuals 5.6e-13 and 3.4e-29), so no argument confined to that piece can rule out 5 in 14; the coupling 56+105 descended to 5.4e-9 on 5 in 14 and was still falling.
findings.status_detail: a numerical search; this is evidence, not proof; no skeptic

findings.statement: All 652 symmetric block-4 skeletons (562 for 2 in 7, 81 for 3 in 10, 4 for 4 in 13, 5 for 7 in 23) are impossible for every choice of complex coefficients.
findings.status_detail: the normalisation fixed the first coefficient of every move to 1 and left out 'first coefficient = 0'; with every coefficient free 4 of 93 sampled skeletons pass the relaxation; 157 of the 562 really cost 5 or 6; the 652 are a sample from one builder

findings.statement: With every coefficient free, 17 of the 652 symmetric block-4 skeletons pass the relaxation (all 2 in 7 at true cost 7); 16 of the 17 have no unit for any complex coefficients (15 exactly over Q; the 16th with its forced zeros modulo two primes); g27_Fany4_s7 is open with 49 of 64 charts excluded exactly and 15 open.
findings.status_detail: exact computation; one AI skeptic rebuilt every system with its own code, found 0 disagreements on 677 relaxations, and independently re-decided 9 of the 15 exact exclusions over Q; five of the other six were only screened at one exact point each, and g27_mid3_m3_s13 was not rechecked

findings.statement: Pattern identity: in each failing symmetric skeleton the target row is a multiple of a few junk rows touched only by the target's own moves; constant multiples give the solver floors 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, polynomial ones give residuals that vanish only as numbers grow; held in 81 of 82 checked certificates, and only where first coefficients are nonzero.
findings.status_detail: no skeptic for the lemma; the 81 of 82 count is the v-nag skeptic's

findings.statement: Choosing letters reaches special position (4 of 1,116 single replacements of a control pass, all exact programs), but all 71 aligned 2-in-7 programs (40 symmetric, 31 asymmetric) that pass the relaxation without dropping a summand fail the full test through the zero divisor (1+u)(1-u) = 0; about 9,400 single and 136 paired letter changes kept it; the one aligned 3-in-10 skeleton fails its relaxation exactly.
findings.status_detail: one program, not repeated by anyone; it inherits the first-coefficient normalisation, so cases with a first coefficient 0 are unchecked

findings.statement: msolve 0.6.5 reads a monomial written x*x as x (exponents not accumulated): {x*x*y*z - x*x, x*x*y*z} gives basis [x], with ^ it gives [x^2]. Write powers as x^k and cross-check with Singular.
findings.status_detail: confirmed by the orchestrating agent on a Colab machine; every affected verdict of these rounds was redone

findings.statement: In the engine game the every-f bound depends only on the block (Corollary F1): the engine group has 96 elements at block 1 and 46,080 at block 2, r' = 12, 20 and at least 28 distinct nonzero traces at blocks 1, 2, 3, and at block 1 f = 1..8 is the shortest range that always suffices; chain shifts have no block-wide bound; with controlled-S the block-2 group is infinite.
findings.status_detail: exact computation; an independent AI skeptic repeated it with its own code (one skeptic) (every number reproduced in exact arithmetic); the general Theorem F behind it is finding 54, argued by hand

findings.statement: 'Some unit saves more than q' is Sigma_1, so s* is computable from below and a true existence claim is provable in Robinson arithmetic: the existence side and every bounded question are never independent; independence can live only in the unbounded ceilings, exactly as far as s* fails to be computable (Theorems A and I). Provability logic, reflection, consistency axioms and large cardinals add no new Sigma_1 truths (Theorem P); Lefschetz principle for fixed shapes.
findings.status_detail: an independent AI skeptic re-derived it and found no error; no person and no proof checker has checked it (one skeptic); item 6 of Theorem A (the full circuit model drops to Sigma_1 exactly when every circuit saving comes from a finite unit) is argued in one direction only

findings.statement: Corollary F1 (finite check of every f in the engine game) replaces the missing Lean lemma of the earlier revisions.
findings.status_detail: its route to 'right at every f' passes through 'a formal identity is right for every f', which is the missing lemma itself

findings.statement: The ml-logic track's dated record (predictions written before computing) is genuine.
findings.status_detail: file times show every file was written within about ten minutes, before most of the times the files give; the mathematics does not depend on it

findings.statement: Proposition D: for each skeleton exactly one of a closure polynomial (a closure-type impossibility proof) or a border curve (an approximate unit, which proves no closure-type proof exists) exists, and searching for both by size decides which. Theorem R, hooks and lifts are narrower than closure-type; for them only the 'no' side is decided.
findings.status_detail: an independent AI skeptic re-derived it and found no error; no person and no proof checker has checked it (one skeptic); corrected from 'rank-type' to 'closure-type'

findings.statement: Three 2-in-7 skeletons at block 4 (g27_Fany4_s5, g27_Fany4_s6, g27_Fp2b_m3_s5) have exact border curves on their relaxations, whose relaxations have no exact solution; one curve refined to 80 digits has relaxation error 0.447 eps while its numbers grow like 0.57/eps.
findings.status_detail: exact computation; an independent AI skeptic repeated it with its own code (one skeptic) (consistent at two new primes; Singular agreed on two; 80-digit Newton refinement); a fourth curve (f27_FAmid3_m3_s16) is numerical only and not reproduced

findings.statement: From the border curves: no Theorem-R certificate can ever exclude 2 in 7 at block 4.
findings.status_detail: the step is incomplete: it needs the border to be right at every f with legitimate letters and the skeleton to lie in the branch the certificate search targets

findings.statement: Refutations of our impossible systems are cheap: 1,304 infeasible relaxations at blocks 3 and 4 and 58 Singular-decided skeletons refute at Nullstellensatz or Polynomial Calculus degree 2 to 6, mostly block + 1; the degree tracks the block, not the moves (2 in 7 and 7 in 23 both at degree 5 at block 4).
findings.status_detail: for the 58 skeletons an AI skeptic redid the degrees exactly over Q (15 at degree 2, 43 at degree 3); the 1,304 were computed modulo a prime only, not repeated

findings.statement: 15 of the 17 two-in-seven relaxations with complex solutions have no solution over the two-element field, so every solution of those 15 must divide by 2.
findings.status_detail: one program, not repeated by anyone

findings.statement: Two-certificate theorem: at a fixed shape exactly one of a refutation identity 1 = sum g_i f_i or a set of commuting rational matrices at which every equation vanishes exists, the matrix size bounded by the product of the degrees (Heintz); so existence at a fixed shape cannot be independent of arithmetic.
findings.status_detail: an independent AI skeptic re-derived it and found no error; no person and no proof checker has checked it (one skeptic) (it confirmed the source)

findings.statement: Six commuting-matrix existence certificates (Karatsuba slice, W-state slice, special-position control, relaxation hits needing i) pass a standalone exact checker; a tampered one is rejected; none is a unit of our problem.
findings.status_detail: exact computation; an independent AI skeptic repeated it with its own code (one skeptic) (including that each certificate belongs to the right original system)

findings.statement: Ruling out every refutation up to the effective-Nullstellensatz degree is hopeless on our systems (about 10^610 unknowns for the smallest real 37-unknown skeleton, 10^(8.7e23) for exact 2 in 7 at block 4, at best 10^357 with structure); plain Bezout counting is blocked (Karatsuba square slice: 1,728 counted, 4 finite); for a square slice with a nonsingular root one prime plus Hensel's lemma proves existence (12 x 12 Karatsuba slice at p = 10007).
findings.status_detail: exact computation; an independent AI skeptic repeated it with its own code (one skeptic)

findings.statement: Four readings of the existence-by-refutation track: 'a proof that an existence proof exists is never cheaper than the existence proof', 'counting is the only non-constructive route', 'counting can prove only border units', 'mod p is never a proof over C'.
findings.status_detail: Hensel lifting, many-primes counts, certified numerics on square slices and refined counting are other routes; the real obstacle is that our systems have more equations than unknowns

findings.statement: 76 of 133 previously undecided skeletons refute at degree 2 or 3 modulo one prime.
findings.status_detail: modulo one prime only, not a proof over C; very likely right but below Singular's verdicts

findings.statement: Every f reduces to finitely many f (Theorem F of the logic round): for letters that act on the digit columns like a finite-state machine (column-uniform letters, chain maps, carries, neighbour phases) a bound N(S) computable from the shape suffices, so each shape is one finite polynomial system decided by Groebner bases.
findings.status_detail: an independent AI skeptic re-derived it and found no error; no person and no proof checker has checked it (one skeptic); its numbers in the engine game are finding 40
